sections.title: Kinds of state, and where each belongs

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this subject, so this part was written for the site, as of October 2026. Frontend libraries change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on a detail.

"Which state library should we use?" is usually the wrong first question. Most state doesn't need one. Sort it by kind first.

| Kind | Examples | Best home |
|---|---|---|
| Local UI | Is this menu open? | `useState` |
| Shared UI | Theme, sidebar, toasts | Context or a small store |
| Server cache | Orders, products, user | TanStack Query or RTK Query |
| URL | Filters, page, tab, selected ID | The router's search params |
| Form | Field values, errors | React Hook Form |
| Persistent preference | Dark mode | localStorage with state |

blocks.title: Choosing where state lives

blocks.text:
Many apps that once needed Redux now need very little global state, because most of it was really a server cache. Removing it is one of the biggest simplifications in modern React.

### URL state

Filters and pagination belong in the URL. Then links can be shared, refresh keeps the view, and the back button works.

blocks.title: Filters in the URL with React Router

blocks.text:
### Keep state minimal

Avoid duplicate and contradictory state. Store `selectedId`, not a copy of the selected object, which goes out of date when the list updates. Calculate the rest during render.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Sort state by kind first
- Server data isn't client state
- Filters belong in the URL
- Store IDs rather than copies
Context solves prop drilling for values that many components need.

blocks.title: A theme context with a safe hook

blocks.text:
Without `useMemo`, the value is a new object each render, and every consumer renders again. The throwing hook gives a clear error when someone forgets the provider. This site's theme works the same way.

### The performance limit

Every component using a context renders when its value changes, even if it uses only one field.

blocks.title: Splitting contexts

blocks.text:
| Good for context | Poor for context |
|---|---|
| Theme, locale | Text being typed |
| Current user | Mouse position |
| Rarely changing settings | Large lists that change often |

Context is a delivery method, and not a state manager in itself. Before reaching for it, consider **composition**: passing components as `children` often removes prop drilling altogether.

blocks.title: Composition removes the middle layers
Key points
blocks.text:
- Memoise a provider's value
- Split contexts by rate of change
- Consumers render on any change
- Try composition first

Server data differs from client state. It's owned elsewhere, can be out of date, and needs caching, refetching, deduplication and error handling. Writing this by hand with `useEffect` means rewriting a library badly.

blocks.title: Setup

blocks.text: ### Reading

blocks.title: useQuery

blocks.text:
You get, for free: caching, sharing between components, request deduplication, retries, refetching when the window regains focus, and cancellation through the signal.

### Stale and cached

| Term | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `staleTime` | How long data counts as fresh | 0: always refetch in the background |
| `gcTime` | How long unused data stays in memory | 5 minutes |
| Fetching | A request is running | |
| Pending | No data yet | |

**Stale-while-revalidate:** show cached data at once, and update it quietly. The default refetching is often more than people expect, so set a sensible `staleTime`.

### Writing

blocks.title: useMutation with cache invalidation

blocks.text:
### Optimistic updates

Show the result at once, and undo it if the server refuses.

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant C as Cache
  participant S as Server
  U->>C: Click like: save old value, update cache
  C-->>U: Shows liked at once
  C->>S: POST /like
  alt success
    S-->>C: OK, refetch to confirm
  else failure
    S-->>C: Error
    C-->>U: Restore old value, show a message
  end
blocks.title: An optimistic update
Optimistic with rollback

blocks.text:
Use it for low-risk actions, such as likes. Don't show money transfers as done before the server confirms.

### Pagination and infinite scroll

Use `useInfiniteQuery` with Spring's `Page` response or a cursor. Prefer a cursor when data changes often, since offset pages shift when rows are added. Spring Data's `Slice` avoids a costly count query for infinite scroll.

**"Why not just useEffect and useState for fetching?"** You'd have to write caching, deduplication, race handling, retries, background refresh and cache invalidation yourself. TanStack Query provides these, and shares data across components with a single key.
blocks.title: Interview answer
Key points
blocks.text:
- Query keys include every input
- Set a sensible staleTime
- Invalidate after writes
- Use optimistic updates only for low-risk actions

When you truly have complex client state, used across the app and changed from many places, use a store: for example an editor, a dashboard builder or a complex multi-step workflow.

### Zustand: small and simple

blocks.title: A store in a few lines
Selecting only what you need

blocks.text:
Selectors solve context's problem: components render only when their selected value changes. There's no provider.

### Redux Toolkit

Redux has one store, actions that describe events, and pure reducers. It's common in large companies, so expect to meet it at work. Redux Toolkit (RTK) is the modern way to write it, and removes the old boilerplate.

blocks.title: A slice
Using it

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
  A[Component] -->|dispatch action| B[Reducer]
  B --> C[New state in store]
  C -->|selector| A
  D[DevTools] -.-> C
blocks.title: One-way data flow in Redux

blocks.text:
### Choosing

| | Context | Zustand | Redux Toolkit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Setup | None | Very small | More |
| Selective re-render | No | Yes | Yes |
| DevTools and time travel | No | Basic, by middleware | Excellent |
| Structure in large teams | Little | Little | Strong conventions |
| Data fetching | No | No | RTK Query |
| Common in | All apps | Newer apps | Large or older apps |

**A sensible default:** TanStack Query for server data, URL for filters, `useState` for local state. Add a store only if something remains that hurts.

**"Redux or Context?"** They solve different problems. Context passes values down, and re-renders all consumers. Redux is a store with selectors, DevTools and structure. I'd first move server data to TanStack Query, as often little remains that needs a global store.
blocks.title: Interview answer
Key points
blocks.text:
- Stores are for complex client state
- Selectors limit re-renders
- RTK removes Redux boilerplate
- Many apps need neither

Most state bugs are modelling bugs. A better shape often removes whole categories of error.

### Booleans become state machines

blocks.title: Booleans allow impossible states
One status with defined transitions

blocks.code:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> editing
  editing --> submitting: SUBMIT
  submitting --> failed: FAIL
  submitting --> done: SUCCEED
  failed --> editing: RETRY
  done --> [*]
blocks.title: The checkout machine

blocks.text:
Now a second SUBMIT while submitting does nothing, which prevents double orders by design. Any unexpected event is ignored. You can test every transition with plain unit tests. The XState library takes this further, though a reducer is enough for most screens.

### A multi-step wizard

blocks.title: Steps as data

blocks.text:
Keep the current step in the URL as well, if the browser's back button should work between steps.

### Normalising

Nested server data leads to deep update code and duplicates.

blocks.title: Nested and normalised

blocks.text:
It's the same idea as database normalisation, which you know from your Databases guide. Redux Toolkit's `createEntityAdapter` helps. You only need this for client-side stores with heavy, interlinked data. A query cache usually avoids it.

### Rules for clean state

| Rule | Example |
|---|---|
| Group related values | `{ x, y }`, rather than two separately changing values |
| Avoid contradictions | One status rather than several booleans |
| Avoid redundancy | Calculate totals |
| Avoid duplication | Keep an ID, not a copy |
| Avoid deep nesting | Flatten, or normalise |

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- One status beats many booleans
- Transitions can prevent double submits
- Reducers test without React
- Normalise only heavy client data

### A query key factory

Scattered string keys go out of step. Keep them in one place.

blocks.title: Keys and options in one module

blocks.text:
Invalidation matches by prefix, so a hierarchy lets you refresh exactly what's needed.

### Dependent and parallel queries

blocks.title: One query waits for another

blocks.text: ### Infinite scroll

blocks.title: useInfiniteQuery with an observer

blocks.text:
On the Spring side, a keyset query such as `WHERE created_at < :cursor ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20` stays fast at any depth, unlike a large `OFFSET`, as your Databases guide explains.

### Prefetching

blocks.code:
<Link
  to={`/orders/${order.id}`}
  onMouseEnter={() => queryClient.prefetchQuery(orderQuery(order.id))}
>
  {order.id}
</Link>
blocks.title: Fetch before the user clicks

blocks.text:
### Updating from a response

If a mutation returns the updated object, write it straight into the cache, rather than refetching.

blocks.title: setQueryData from a response

blocks.text: ### Global error handling

blocks.title: One place for query errors

blocks.text:
The default retry policy retries failed queries three times with backoff, which makes a 404 look slow. Skip retries for client errors.

### Common mistakes

| Mistake | Result | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Missing a variable in the key | Shows the wrong data | Include every input |
| Copying query data into `useState` | Goes stale | Use `data` directly |
| Fetching in `useEffect` and caching by hand | Duplicate logic | Use a query |
| No `staleTime` | Too many refetches | Set one for each kind of data |
| Sharing a `QueryClient` across users on a server | Data leaks | One per request in SSR |

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Keep keys in a factory
- enabled makes queries dependent
- Use a cursor for infinite scroll
- Don't retry 4xx errors
#### Kinds of state, and where each belongs

items.question: Why store a selected order's ID rather than the object?
items.answer: A copy goes stale when the list updates. Derive the object from the ID and the list.

items.question: Why put search filters in the URL?
items.answer: Links are shareable, refresh keeps them, and back and forward work.

blocks.text: #### Context, and its limits

items.question: Why might every consumer render even though the data hasn't changed?
items.answer: The provider's value is a new object each render. Memoise it.

items.question: Context holds user and cart. Adding to the cart renders the avatar. How do you fix it?
items.answer: Split into two contexts, or use a store with selectors.

blocks.text: #### Server state with TanStack Query

items.question: Two components use the same query key. How many requests are sent?
items.answer: One. Requests are deduplicated, and both share the cached result.

items.question: After a mutation, the list shows old data. What's missing?
items.answer: Invalidate the related query keys, or update the cache.

items.question: What does staleTime: 0 cause when you return to the tab?
items.answer: A background refetch, since data counts as stale immediately.

blocks.text: #### Redux Toolkit and Zustand

items.question: Why does RTK allow state.items.push inside a reducer?
items.answer: Immer records the changes on a draft, and produces a new immutable state.

items.question: Why might a Zustand selector perform better than context?
items.answer: A component renders only when its selected value changes, rather than on any change.

items.question: An app has Redux full of API data and loading flags. What would you suggest?
items.answer: Move server data to TanStack Query or RTK Query, leaving only real client state.

blocks.text: #### Modelling state well

items.question: How does a state machine prevent double submits?
items.answer: In the submitting state, a SUBMIT event has no transition, so it's ignored.

items.question: Why is one status better than isLoading, isError and isSuccess?
items.answer: Booleans allow impossible combinations. A single status can only be one thing at a time.

blocks.text: #### Advanced TanStack Query

items.question: Two filters show the same results. What's the likely bug?
items.answer: The filter isn't in the query key, so both use one cache entry.

items.question: Why does a 404 take several seconds to show an error?
items.answer: Default retries with backoff. Skip retries for client errors.

items.question: How do you refresh order lists but not an order's details?
items.answer: Invalidate by a hierarchical key prefix, such as `['orders', 'list']`.
